Task 1 — complete k3s vendoring + registry probe (was 10s3 Task 3)
------------------------------------------------------------------
1a. Check whether content/vendor/k3s/ exists and versions.lock has
    k3s entries. If present and complete, verify sha256s and skip to
    1d. If absent, do the full vendoring:
      - pin the latest STABLE k3s release
        (github.com/k3s-io/k3s/releases) — record version + URLs +
        sha256 in versions.lock
      - fetch into content/vendor/k3s/:
          k3s binary (linux amd64)
          install.sh (https://get.k3s.io)
          k3s-selinux RPM (rpm.rancher.io) — REQUIRED on RHEL with
          SELinux enforcing; if the fetch fails, record it as a
          DECISION POINT for 11r (install --disable-selinux vs
          sourcing the RPM another way). Do not silently drop it.
          k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst for the pinned version
          (~300MB — commit it; determinism beats repo size)
1b. REGISTRY PROBE (informs script 62's pull strategy): read the
    exact system-image tags for the pinned k3s release
    (mirrored-pause, mirrored-coredns-coredns,
    local-path-provisioner, klipper-helm, klipper-lb,
    mirrored-library-busybox — from the release docs), and probe
    each via $DOCKER_REGISTRY/v2/<image-path>/manifests/<tag> with
    the manifest Accept header. Report a table: image | tag | code.
1c. Record in versions.lock: k3s version, all sha256s, probe outcome.
1d. Note for 11r in the probe outcome: ctr does NOT honour
    registries.conf mirrors — script 62 uses explicit
    $DOCKER_REGISTRY pulls + k3s ctr images tag to the original name
    regardless of probe results; the probe tells us whether the
    mirror COULD serve these (warm-cache confidence) either way.

Task 4 — curated.json finalisation
----------------------------------
4a. Ensure the OpenTelemetry k3s-dependent entry exists per 10s3
    Task 2c (it appears to be missing):
      { "name": "otel-manifest", "requires_k3s": true,
        "exec": "kubectl",
        "steps": [ "kubectl apply -f <vendored app_pod.yaml path>",
                   "kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l <label
                    read from the vendored manifest> --timeout=120s
                    -n <namespace read from the manifest>",
                   "kubectl port-forward --address 127.0.0.1 <pod>
                    18080:<containerPort from the manifest>" ],
        "check": { "url": "http://localhost:18080/...", "expect":
                   confirmed-from-lab-or {"type":"running"} } }
    Port 18080 is collision-free by design (perses:8080,
    fluentbit:9999, docs:8090, prometheus:9090, jaeger:16686).
    Namespace/labels/ports come FROM the vendored manifest — read,
    do not invent. Record all deviations in exec_adaptations.
4b. Audit every curated entry: exec_adaptations present and
    complete; source.raw quoted; check expectation confirmed from
    docs/HTML or downgraded to {"type":"running"} WITH the reason.
4c. Regenerate curated.json. EVERY track must have: >=1 podman/dock
    run entry AND (otel additionally) the k3s entry.
